title: Fretboard wood: ComfyUI textures against procedural TSL, and texture memory
question: For the fretboard's wood, what do a 2048x2048 texture (from the ComfyUI GA lab's experiment 4, seamless woods), the same texture compressed to KTX2, and a procedural wood written in TSL cost in GPU memory and GPU time?
hypothesis: An RGBA8 texture with mipmaps holds about 4/3 x 4 bytes per texel; a GPU-compressed KTX2 (BC7 on this GPU) holds a quarter of that; the procedural wood holds nothing but costs noise evaluations per pixel.

predictions.metric: GPU memory of the KTX2 (UASTC transcoded to BC7)
median GPU ms per frame, procedural TSL against the sampled texture, board filling a 1920x1080 frame

predictions.predicted: pending if R2 has not run the ComfyUI GA lab's experiment 4 when this runs
